subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Uneven Roasting
description: A quick, practical guide to Uneven Roasting.

hook.text: Break open a poorly roasted bean and you might find the outside is brown while the inside is still pale and raw.

buildup.text: Uneven roasting means heat didn't penetrate uniformly. The surface over-developed while the core under-developed.

discovery.text: This creates a mix of sour (raw center) and bitter (over-roasted exterior) flavors in the same cup—a chaotic taste.

twist.text: Uneven roasting often comes from inconsistent bean size. Large and small beans in the same batch develop at different rates.

climax.text: Screen-grading green coffee (sorting by size) before roasting is a simple fix that dramatically improves consistency.

punchline.text: Same batch, different roasts inside every bean. Sorting solves this.

quiz.question: What causes uneven roasting within a single bean?
options: Heat didn't penetrate uniformly—surface over-roasted, core under-developed

details.summary: Uneven roasting produces beans that range in color from light to dark within the same batch. Causes include inconsistent bean size, poor drum rotation, overloading, or fluctuating heat. The result is an unpredictable cup that mixes sour and bitter notes.
details.whyItMatters: Consistency is the hallmark of a professional roast. Even small variations within a batch reduce sweetness and create confusing flavors in the cup.
takeaways: Mixed bean colors in one batch signal uneven roasting
Causes include overloading, poor agitation, and size variation
Uneven roasts produce cups that mix sour and bitter flavors

faq.question: How can roasters check for uneven roasting after a batch?
faq.answer: Spread a sample of the cooled beans on a white surface and look for color variation. Even a slight range from tan to dark brown indicates uneven development. Agtron colorimeters provide precise numerical measurements.

faq.question: Does bean density affect roast evenness within a batch?
faq.answer: Yes. Beans from different altitudes or varieties within the same lot can have different densities, causing them to absorb heat at different rates. Sorting by screen size and density before roasting improves uniformity.
